text:
Devon Toews already has six goals, double last season's total, and 19 points in 21 games. Denver has noticed: the Avalanche outscore opponents heavily with him on the ice, and they get 58.7% of the expected goals at five on five, more than nine points better than without him. His minutes have climbed too, over 23 a night across his last ten games, including 29 in an overtime loss in Ottawa.

Here's the honest part. Some of this won't last. He's shooting 16% after 3% last season, against a league norm around 6% for defensemen, and the Avs have scored 9.5 more goals than expected with him out there. His scoring rate of 2.5 points per 60 is far above our talent range of 1.1 to 1.6. We'd expect the goals to slow.

The process underneath is good, though. Evolving-Hockey had him in the 94th percentile among defensemen for driving offense last season (with very strong teammates, which flatters the raw numbers), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking ranked him in the 97th percentile for chances from in front of the net. A bounce-back, yes. Just not quite this big.
